text: When you work with APIs, you send HTTP requests to a server to get or send data. The server usually responds with JSON, a simple text format that is easy for computers to read. Before making requests, you often need authentication, like an API key, to prove who you are. Many APIs also have rate limits, meaning you can only make a certain number of requests per minute. If you exceed this, you may get an error. That’s why error handling is important: your code should be ready for problems like bad responses or expired keys, so you can fix them quickly and keep your app running smoothly.
